triage.reason: The motor stopped 13 ms after the pinch force passed 100 N. The limit is 10 ms (9.0 V, -30 °C), so a pinch is not stopped in time.

Retained power after ignition off ends at about 50 s, but the reporter expects 60 s. A limit is missed with no safety effect, and turning the ignition back on is a workaround. The reporter is unsure of the spec value, so this needs checking.
WLC_Status period of 97-104 ms is within 100 ms ±10 ms. Logged for information only.
False pinch reversal during express close at about -20 °C with nothing in the way. Closing works wrongly in normal cold-weather use.
Comment typo only. The code is correct.
Same problem: pinch stop is late (14 ms) at -30 °C and low supply.

Sleep current is 140 µA against a 100 µA limit, probably because the CAN transceiver stays in standby instead of sleep. A limit is missed with no safety effect. The fix may need a change in the transceiver mode handling.
False reversal caused by road vibration (2 of 10 tries). This is a different cause from the cold-weather false reversal in DR-1004, so it is not a duplicate.
Overcurrent stops the motor, but B1A02 is not stored and the fault state stays 0. The diagnostic function is lost.
Too vague to judge: a subjective clinic comment with no measurement. The severity is provisional. The switch-to-motor reaction time needs to be measured.
Same problem: false reversal during auto-up in cold weather (-18 °C) with no obstacle.
The thermal block lets one open request through after the model passes 140 °C, which looks like an off-by-one. This protects the motor, not people, so a limit is missed with no safety effect.
Position drifts 3.5 mm at the top seal after 200 cycles, so position is wrong in normal use. Check whether the drift moves the anti-pinch active zone near the seal; if it does, raise to S1.

At 16 V the motor keeps running 180 ms after switch release. The limit is 100 ms, and at 13.5 V it is 60 ms. A limit is missed, and anti-pinch stays active during the overrun. The voltage dependence suggests checking the switch input reading at high supply.
Same problem: retained power after ignition off is shorter than 60 s (about 45 s here).
One WLC_Status frame was lost during heavy diagnostic load (200 ms gap). This is rare and has no safety effect.
Documentation error in the owner's manual. No WLC-200 design change is needed. The component is assigned only by nearest topic.
Hall signal loss is not detected (sensor plausibility check). The motor runs on to the end stop with no position feedback, so anti-pinch is effectively bypassed. No DTC is stored.
Same problem: the thermal block above 140 °C lets one opening through.
Express close works when the window is not normalized. Without valid position, pinch protection cannot work reliably, so a safety function can be bypassed.
Unused variable that causes a compiler warning. Cosmetic code-quality issue.
Diagnostic response takes 55-62 ms against a 50 ms limit, in 3% of requests during motor start. This is rare and has no safety effect.
Same problem: false reversal on cobblestone road while closing.
Reverse polarity at -14 V destroys protection diode D3 and the controller is dead afterwards. The function is lost.
Undervoltage stop in 21 ms is within the 50 ms limit. Information only.
Loud knock at the top seal with no damage. This is a subjective comfort issue in end-stop behaviour and needs measurement of end-stop current and speed.
Same problem from a different test: Hall loss is not detected, the motor keeps running into the seal, and no DTC is stored.
Inrush current of 14 A has no spec limit, so this is not a failure. It is a proposal for a new requirement.
Same problem: on overcurrent the fault state stays 0 and no DTC is stored.
